about: Conformance vectors for Starcom's PsiLines and the shared window profile (the delegation plan, docs/plans/2026-10-25-psiops-rlsh-delegation.md 3.2, 3.4 and 3.6), from Mecha Jono's reference (beu/psi_lines.py). Fixed inputs: re-running gives the same bytes.

engine.name: skyfield
engine.timescale: skyfield built-in (its Delta T and UT1 tables)

time_scale: UTC, Unix seconds (leap seconds not counted, as JavaScript Date.getTime() / 1000)

conventions.place: apparent geocentric RA and Dec of date: light time, annual aberration and gravitational deflection, true equator and equinox of date (skyfield earth.at(t).observe(body).apparent().radec(epoch='date')); nutation IAU 2000A
conventions.sidereal: Greenwich apparent sidereal time (GAST), from UT1. GMST in its place moves every line by the equation of the equinoxes: 0.0021 to 0.0029 degrees at these instants, never more than about 0.0048, below the 0.05 tolerance, so the vectors cannot tell the two apart; GAST is the one that goes with an RA of date
conventions.asc_dsc: H0 = arccos(-tan(lat) tan(dec)) where |tan(lat) tan(dec)| <= 1; asc = wrap180(RA - GAST - H0) (rising), dsc = wrap180(RA - GAST + H0) (setting); none (null) where -tan(lat) tan(dec) < -1 (circumpolar) or > 1 (never rises)
conventions.geocentric: no parallax: the Moon's lines are its geocentric lines. Its MC and IC hold on the ground too (on the meridian, parallax moves it along the meridian only); its ASC and DSC are about 1 degree from the topocentric horizon
conventions.horizon: geometric, altitude 0: no refraction, no semidiameter
conventions.speed_fraction: stations carry [profile, speed_fraction, half, cap] (the speed as a fraction of the body's mean motion: half weight at half, the window's edge at cap). No weights vector: Starcom draws the window band from the event's start to its end (the window tag's from and until; t_in and t_out here) with its peak at exact

profile_weights.about: Each case: the profile tag exactly as the wire carries it (every element a string), the window (start, end) in seconds from the anchor (gauss_orb, past_boundary: the exact time; rise_halflife: the recurrence anchor) where w is above zero, and samples [tau_s, w].

rules.gauss_orb: [profile, gauss_orb, h_deg, cap_deg, rate_deg_per_day, accel_deg_per_day2]: orb(tau) = rate d + accel d^2 / 2 with d = tau / 86400; w = exp(-ln2 (orb / h)^2) while |orb| <= cap on the contiguous span around tau = 0, else 0. Inside the cap includes the cap itself (w there is 2^-((cap/h)^2), 0.00195 at cap 3h).
rules.rise_halflife: [profile, rise_halflife, lead_min, peak_min, half_life_min, end_min]: w = 0 before -lead; linear from 0 at -lead to 1 at the peak; then 2^(-(tau - peak) / half_life), set to 0 where it falls below 0.05 or past the end.
rules.past_boundary: [profile, past_boundary, h_deg, cap_deg, rate_deg_per_day]: orb(tau) = |rate| tau / 86400, the travel past the boundary, negative before exactness (the applying side) whichever way the body moves; w = 0 for orb < 0, exp(-ln2 (orb / h)^2) for 0 <= orb <= cap, 0 past the cap. Computed by beu/psi_lines.py (beu/window_search.py has no such kind).

profile_weights.edges: No sample sits exactly on a discontinuity except tau = 0 of past_boundary, where w = 1 (0 <= orb is inclusive), with -1 s and +1 s beside it to pin its two sides; every other sample is at least a minute from an edge.

cases.name: moon_pair
cases.about: a Moon pair: h 1, cap 3, 12.19 degrees a day (06 2.3)

cases.name: sun_venus_like
cases.about: a Sun or inner-planet pair: h 2, cap 6, 1.2 degrees a day

cases.name: slow_outer_accel
cases.about: a slow outer pair with acceleration: h 1, cap 3, 0.02 degrees a day, 0.00004 a day a day (the window is asymmetric)

cases.name: rlsh_title_night
cases.about: an RLSH title night: lead 120 min, peak 0, half-life 60 min, end 360 min (the 0.05 cut comes first, at 259.3 min)

cases.name: rlsh_long_lead
cases.about: a long lead: lead 1440 min, peak 120 min, half-life 90 min, end 300 min (the end cuts first, at 0.25)

cases.name: moon_ingress
cases.about: a Moon ingress: h 1, cap 1, 14.7 degrees a day

cases.name: slow_ingress
cases.about: a slow ingress: h 1, cap 1, 0.5 degrees a day

cases.name: slow_ingress_retrograde
cases.about: the same, retrograde (rate -0.5): past the boundary is after exactness whichever way the body moves, so the weights are the direct case's

angular.about: For each instant: GAST (degrees), skyfield's Delta T (TT - UT1) and UT1 - UTC (seconds) there, and each body's apparent RA and Dec of date with its MC and IC longitudes. Tolerances: mc_lon and ic_lon 0.05 degrees; ra_deg, dec_deg and gast_deg 0.01 degrees, to localise a disagreement.

horizon_curves.about: For each instant and body: at each latitude (geodetic, -66 to 66 every 6), the ASC (rising) and DSC (setting) longitudes on the geometric horizon; both null where the body is circumpolar or never rises, with that state named. Tolerance 0.05 degrees in longitude. edge_cases: the Sun and the Moon at -80, -72, 72 and 80, where the nulls are (none of the grid's points is null at these instants).

aspect_times.about: Events from Mecha Jono's sky-event catalogue (beu/psi_catalogue.py) over the span, for Starcom's own search of the same event. The check is the angle: at our exact_utc, your defining angle minus target_deg is within 60 arcsec (1', astronomy-engine's own stated accuracy). Equivalently your exact time is within the event's tolerance_s (60 arcsec at its rate: about 2 minutes for the Moon, days for a slow pair). A station has no tolerance_s: check its body's speed changes sign within 1 hour of exact_utc. t_in and t_out are where the orb crosses orb_cap (the window's edges); rate and accel are the defining angle's, in degrees a day and a day a day.
aspect_times.frame: geocentric apparent ecliptic longitudes of date (true ecliptic and equinox of date, skyfield ecliptic_frame): light time, aberration and deflection; DE440s; nutation IAU 2000B (the catalogue's; within about 1 mas of 2000A). Never the J2000 ecliptic: exact_j2000_utc, where given, is the same crossing in the J2000 ecliptic, to tell a frame mix-up from an ephemeris difference (here up to 221 s apart: Uranus-Pluto, 2026-11-29).

rules.aspect: exact where wrap180(lon(bodies[0]) - lon(bodies[1]) - target_deg) = 0; target_deg = 360 k / n or 360 - 360 k / n (each side of the circle is its own event); rate is d/dt of that difference
rules.lunation: the Sun-Moon aspect at 0 (new), 180 (full), 270 (first quarter: the Moon 90 ahead of the Sun) or 90 (last quarter) in lon(Sun) - lon(Moon)
rules.station: exact where d lon / dt of the body crosses zero (retrograde: + to -; direct: - to +); target_deg holds the body's longitude there
rules.arcsec_in_60s: how far the defining angle moves in 60 s at this rate
rules.tolerance_s: the time 60 arcsec of the defining angle is worth at this rate: the time check that is the same as the angle check

aspect_times.selection: every lunation, eclipse and station in the span; the Moon's first conjunction with each of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto; then the major aspects (harmonics 1, 2, 3, 4, 6) between the Sun and the planets, in time order; at most 40, listed in time order
